content:
nate: FYI discovered in partner CI logs: plaintext `backup_key_secret` value and several KMS-wrapped blobs referenced. Logs were in a public artifact for ~12h.
claire: how sensitive is `backup_key_secret`? is it a root key or just an application secret?
nate: looks like an envelope-encrypted data key material used by their backup tool. not the CMK, but if they have the unwrapped data key it can decrypt backups. also found `kms_ciphertext: AQICAH...` entries.
diego: do we have evidence of the key being used by unknown principals? CloudTrail shows Decrypt calls from partner account and one anomalous decrypt from an ip in europe 10 hours ago.
sam: partner says their CI runner uploaded artifacts inadvertently; they've already removed the artifact. but we have to assume exfiltration.
ops-oncall: I created an incident: #INC-2026-9123. Locked partner artifact storage and disabled public access.
sec-bot: Incident created and channel created for coordination. severity: high initially given potential plaintext key.
claire: immediate ask: can we rotate the CMK used to encrypt those data keys or rotate the data keys at partner side? which is lower blast radius?
diego: options: 1) rotate CMK (rekey) - breaks all ciphertext encrypted by that CMK unless re-encrypt performed; 2) revoke partner IAM decrypt permissions then re-encrypt allowed objects with new CMK and give partner a short-lived decrypt role; 3) rotate the application-level data keys inside backups (requires restoring and re-encrypting backups) - heavy.
nate: lean towards option 2 (revoke perms -> re-encrypt -> ephemeral decrypt). less downtime for customers.
sam: need to coordinate partner deployment window. they run nightly restore jobs; any mismatch will fail. recommend a canary restore.
ops-oncall: I've created a temporary kms role `partner-temporary-decrypt` with 1hr max session, bound to partner's OIDC client. created PR to allow sts:AssumeRole from partner OIDC.
claire: good. we'll also add a key policy statement that requires `aws:RequestTag/rotation=2026-09-xx` so only re-encrypt jobs with that tag can succeed during the window.
diego: sample re-encrypt command we used for earlier incidents:
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://old_blob.bin \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222:key/new-cmk-id \
  --output text > new_blob.bin
```
nate: note: partner CI tooling expects the envelope header to have `X-Env-Version:1`. preserve that when writing new ciphertext. do a canary object.
sam: I'll coordinate canary restore at +50m. partner confirmed engineer available.
ops-oncall: performing permission revoke on partner's decrypt role now (temporary deny). ETA 2m.
sec-bot: Action recorded: revoked decrypt permission from `arn:aws:iam::222333:role/partner-access`.
claire: while we do this, enable CloudTrail log export for Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/Encrypt events to our secure audit bucket with Object Lock enabled. we want immutable evidence.
diego: adding a CloudWatch alarm for >3 Decrypt calls from non-whitelisted IPs over 15m.
nate: post-containment: we should require partner to rotate application-level secrets and stop embedding secrets in CI logs. add pre-commit hook and CI redact step.
sam: remind partner to use KMS GenerateDataKey without printing the plaintext to logs. and to leverage KMS Grant for short-lived decrypt.
ops-oncall: re-encrypt run started for canary blob. copying `canary/backup1.enc` -> `rotated/backup1.enc`.
claire: also open a Vault ticket: propose partner migrate to Vault transit for data-key orchestration. Vault can issue ephemeral data keys and audit every decrypt. long-term must be Vault or KMS grants with ephemeral sessions.
diego: IAM minimization plan: update key policy to require `kms:EncryptionContext:purpose=backup` and `aws:PrincipalTag/environment=partner` for all decrypts from partner principals. that will make leaked ciphertexts unusable outside intended context.
nate: good. we should also add a condition requiring `aws:RequestTag/nonce` to be present for decrypt calls triggered by partner CI (enforced by wrapper).
sam: canary decrypt succeeded. partner performed restore of one file using new_blob.bin. success verified by checksum.
ops-oncall: rolling full re-encrypt now. will stage `rotated/` objects and then switch partner config to new key alias `alias/backup-rotated-2026-09` during the maintenance window.
sec-bot: Incident update: severity reduced to medium after canary success and decrypt revoke.
claire: followups and owners:
- nate: draft partner disclosure + recommended checklist (redact CI, rotate app secrets, pre-commit ignore)
- diego: open PR for key-policy changes + IAM conditions
- ops-oncall: finish re-encrypt and rotate alias; validate no failed restores in next 2 hours
- sam: work with partner on CI sanitization and a vault migration plan
- sec-bot: attach CloudTrail export and incident timeline
nate: creating post-incident ticket and will include recommended timeline and sample policies. will ask legal to coordinate required disclosure.
diego: one more item: enable KMS key rotation (automatic yearly) for that CMK and require periodic key-rotation policy in partner contracts.
ops-oncall: re-encrypt complete. updated alias to `alias/backup-rotated-2026-09`. partner config rolled.
sec-bot: Incident #INC-2026-9123 monitoring for 24h. logs exported to `s3://redwood-secure-audit/incidents/7453212345/`.
sam: will run a restore sweep to catch hidden failures; partner to run test restores nightly for 3 days.
claire: also add an automated scanner to detect strings that look like base64-encoded data keys in CI artifacts; create alert to eng-security.
nate: thanks everyone. closing loop after partner postmortem in 48h. :rocket:
